description:
FILED s431 (Opus 5), found while minimising #464 (the Test2::Formatter::TAP line is `local($\, $,) = (undef, '') if $\ || $,;` -- the same line carries both bugs).

    print defined($\) ? "d\n" : "u\n";   perl u    PCL d     <- WRONG
    print defined($,) ? "d\n" : "u\n";   perl u    PCL d     <- WRONG
    print defined($/) ? "d\n" : "u\n";   perl d    PCL d     (right)
    print defined($;) ? "d\n" : "u\n";   perl d    PCL d     (right)
    print defined($!) ? "d\n" : "u\n";   perl d    PCL d     (right)

perl's defaults: `$\` (output record separator) and `$,` (output field
separator) are UNDEF until set; `$/` is "\n", `$;` is "\034", `$!` is the
errno object.  PCL initialises all five to a defined value, so every
`if $\`, `defined $,`, `$, // ","` guard answers the wrong way -- and the
output itself is unaffected, which is what makes it silent.

BAR: the five rows above + the write path (`$, = ":"; print 1,2` and
`$\ = "!\n"; print "x"` must keep working), `local $\ = undef` inside a block,
and the `$OFS`/`$ORS` English aliases if they exist; a Pl/t guard row of the
oracle form.  Runtime-only (the defvar initialisation in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp),
so the full sweep is NOT optional (CLAUDE.md WHAT-TO-RUN table, cl/** row).


DONE s441c (agent C, Opus; merged by Fable s440 as 76f5de7). cl/pcl-runtime.lisp: |$\| and |$,| initialise to *p-undef*. p-print's two readers test "a non-empty string", never `defined`, so the write path is byte-identical -- probed: `$,` between args, `$\` after the list, printf never appending `$\`, `local $\ = ...` / bare `local $,` / restore across a sub call, `$"` interpolation. Guard Pl/t/sep-vars-01.t (4 differential rows; 3 fail on a base tree, the write-path row passes on both by design). docs/ir-spec.md sec. 8 records the asymmetry as normative. NOT done, and filed: $OFS/$ORS are unreachable because `use English` dies transpiling core English.pm (#502); PCL emits no warnings-gated diagnostic (#221's class) -- perl does NOT warn for print with an undef separator, probed, so the OUTPUT matches. New finding: `say` appends `$\` where perl uses "\n" instead -- #500. Runtime change -> the sweep runs with the s441 batch (Fable).
